To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
motion in a picture can change the emotional response profile, and that the change is consistent with the motion being a signal of potential danger or reward.

1) moving pictures elicit stronger emotional reactions than still pictures, 2) this effect is independent of the content of the picture, and 3) this effect is mediated through the arousal dimension of emotion.
motion increases arousal, does not affect valence, and sustains the viewer's attention to the stimulus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the medium and the medium's attributes on the processing and perception of emotion.

the role of emotion processing in three systems (the medium, the message, and the message modulator) and the impact of the interaction between the three systems on emotion experience and physiological response.
the role of the medium and message in emotional processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the motion in an image can be used to increase the arousal of a viewer and can also be used to capture and sustain the attention of the viewer.
motion is a powerful and specific attribute that increases arousal and attention, and does not affect the quality of the induced emotional state.
the addition of motion to a picture has an impact on the emotion response pattern that is consistent with the impact of arousal on the emotion response profile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impact of motion in the context of emotion processing is not a simple one.
motion has an impact on the emotional response profile that can be described as a general arousal amplifier.
the medium (motion) is more important than the message (emotion content) in the context of picture presentation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stimulus motion is an effective way to increase the intensity of an emotion response without altering the quality of that response.
the formal properties of a stimulus presentation can have a profound effect on the emotional response it elicits.
motion is an important attribute of emotion eliciting stimuli and that its effects are specific and systematic.
